stages_checked.position: BEFORE noise layer (operates on raw OCR blocks)
stages_checked.detail: structure_freeze_stage receives `normalized_blocks` (OCR block dicts with normalized_text). It freezes option structures before question splitting. The noise layer operates on `questions` (parsed question dicts with `stem` fields). These are completely different data types at different pipeline phases. structure_freeze has already completed and its output is immutable (MappingProxy-wrapped) before the noise layer ever runs.

normalize_schema transforms raw OCR blocks into structured question dicts with `stem`, `options`, `answer` fields. The noise layer runs AFTER normalize_schema completes, modifying stems. normalize_schema is a preceding stage; its work is done before the noise layer starts.

The noise layer removes OCR artifacts BEFORE code structure reconstruction. This REDUCES the number of false-positive code integrity flags because noise lines like (1> can be mistaken for code issues. In all test cases, code integrity was preserved or improved. The noise layer acts as a pre-filter that reduces unnecessary LLM calls in code_structure_reconstruct.

stages_checked.position: BEFORE noise layer (raw blocks -> split questions)
stages_checked.detail: question_splitter operates on raw OCR blocks during the split phase, which happens BEFORE normalize_schema. The noise layer runs AFTER normalize_schema. These are completely different pipeline phases with no shared mutable state.
